title: Decision and Use-Case Specification
purpose: Define the service problem, full intervention, realistic comparators, outcomes, value mechanism, decision rule, and review cycle.
notes: Synthetic example. Replace all values with authorized local evidence before institutional use.

records.Guidance: Describe the unmet clinical, operational, workforce, quality, accreditation, or public-health need using measurable baseline evidence.
records.Institutional response: Median emergency-department time to clinical prioritization is 42 minutes; 18% of high-risk patients wait longer than the local target.

records.Guidance: Define included and excluded populations, services, locations, and time periods.
records.Institutional response: Adults in two urban emergency departments; pediatric, obstetric, and major-trauma pathways excluded from the initial pilot.

records.Guidance: Describe the complete intervention bundle: data, model, interfaces, thresholds, users, review, workflow, downstream action, monitoring, support, and exit.
records.Institutional response: Version-controlled risk service using EHR data, nurse confirmation, documented override, escalation, monitoring, and rollback.

records.Guidance: Record current practice, process redesign, staffing, equipment, conventional digital tools, alternative AI, shared service, and no-change options where relevant.
records.Institutional response: Current triage, revised streaming, additional triage staffing, and a non-AI early-warning score.

records.Guidance: Identify the authority making the decision and the hospital, health-system, payer, patient, societal, or combined perspective.
records.Institutional response: Hospital executive committee; hospital and health-system perspectives with patient and environmental effects reported separately.

records.Guidance: Define clinical, operational, quality, accreditation, workforce, economic, equity, trust, environmental, and safety outcomes.
records.Institutional response: Time to assessment, missed deterioration, false-alert burden, workload, subgroup access, staff experience, lifecycle cost, and continuity.

records.Guidance: State the analytic horizon and the time within which an output must lead to action.
records.Institutional response: Three-year economic horizon; output must arrive within five minutes of triage documentation.

records.Guidance: Explain how the intervention is expected to change a decision, action, outcome, resource consequence, and public value.
records.Institutional response: Earlier identification changes escalation timing, reduces avoidable harm, and preserves scarce response capacity.

records.Guidance: Define proceed, redesign, silent validation, pilot, conditional adoption, scale, restrict, pause, replace, or retire criteria.
records.Institutional response: Proceed to silent-mode validation only if data completeness exceeds 95%, subgroup calibration is acceptable, and fallback is tested.

records.Guidance: Record the last evidence date, responsible reviewer, planned review date, and trigger events.
records.Institutional response: Evidence cut-off 2026-01-31; owner Director of Quality; next review 2026-07-31 or upon material change.
